_note: What people commonly RUN at each width — NOT a menu of what is orderable. Forged wheels are cut to the truck and the brands publish no ET, so this exists so the page can answer 'what offset?' with something real instead of silence. Every number carries its source. A width with no reliable public figure gets an explicit null, never a guess.
_note_shape: Keyed on ROLE + WIDTH, not per model. Offset is set by rim width and axle position, not by spoke design — keying per model would be 756 copies of the same handful of numbers. The {min,max,typical} shape matches f450-fitment.json's rear.offsetMm so Fitment.geometry() could consume it unchanged.
_note_bySize: An override layer for observed data points, not the primary key. 22x12 at -44 and 24x12 at -51 are two separate listings, not a rule about 12-inch wheels.
